title: Coordinator run state
description: state.json. A mutable snapshot of where a run is, rewritten on every transition. It deliberately holds no event log: history.jsonl owns that, so a torn state write cannot take the audit trail with it.

phase.description: Where the run is now. Every coordinator has one, which is what lets a single status envelope describe all of them.

history.description: Rejected outright. Present only in version 1 runs, where it was the bug that motivated the split.

execution_plan_sha256.description: The digest execution is bound to. Distinct from plan_sha256 so a plan edited after binding is detectable rather than silently adopted.

applied.description: Scope-relative paths of the mutating operations the agent actually carried out, verified against the filesystem before being recorded.

manifest_sha256.description: Digest of the proposed manifest, so approval binds to the exact plan that was reviewed rather than to whatever the file says later.

mode.description: Whether the run may modify its scope or only describe it. Mirrors the --mode choices, so a state file cannot claim a mode the CLI cannot produce.

mutating_count.description: How many of those operations modify the scope. Zero is what makes an approval gate unnecessary.

name.description: The subject's slug, for coordinators whose subject is a name rather than an existing skill directory.

operation_count.description: Operations in the bound manifest, carried so status can describe the run's size without re-reading it.

run_id.description: Identifies which run wrote a provenance record, so records from a re-run are distinguishable from the run that produced them.

scope.description: Root of the tree a run may modify. Bound at init so a later phase cannot quietly widen it.

scopeExtension.description: A mid-merge widening of the mutable path set. Reasoned and recorded, because the alternative to allowing it is a full rebind, which makes the safe route the expensive one.

approval.description: A human's approval of one exact manifest. Binding it to the digest is what stops an approved run from executing a manifest nobody reviewed.
